sentences.text: This study investigated how removing lipid signals and varying the frequency range affect chemical measurements in rat brains scanned at 14.1 Tesla.

Researchers applied orthogonal projection, a mathematical method for signal removal, to data sets with low or high lipid interference, analyzing chemical signals across both wide and narrow frequency ranges.
While lipid removal caused only small changes in data with little interference, it significantly altered chemical maps and concentration estimates in data with heavy lipid interference.
Chemicals present in very small amounts were most impacted by this process, and similar patterns of change appeared in data sets using a faster, compressed sensing scanning technique.
